```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkad394>
* Citation: Olsson A, Malmberg C, Zhao C, Friberg LE, Nielsen EI, Lagerback P,
  Tangden T. Synergy of polymyxin B and minocycline against KPC-3- and
  OXA-48-producing *Klebsiella pneumoniae* in dynamic time-kill experiments:
  agreement with in silico predictions. *J Antimicrob Chemother*
  2024;79(2):391-402. PMCID: PMC10832586.

This is **not** a population PK model. It is a semi-mechanistic
pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of bacterial killing by
polymyxin B (PMB) and minocycline (MIN), alone and in combination, against
carbapenem-resistant *Klebsiella pneumoniae*. The structural model is that of
Zhao et al. 2020 (*Int J Antimicrob Agents* 55:105941), which Olsson 2024
reproduces in supplementary Table S1 (equations 1-10) with the parameter
values in Table 3.

The model has two bacterial states: a growing drug-susceptible population
(`bact_susceptible`, S) that transfers to a resting drug-insusceptible
population (`bact_resting`, R) as the total count approaches the system
carrying capacity `Bmax`. Each drug kills the susceptible bacteria through a
power function of its concentration, attenuated by a drug-specific,
*irreversible* adaptive-resistance system (an `aroff` -> `aron` transition
whose rate rises with concentration). Polymyxin B enhances minocycline twice
over: it raises the minocycline kill rate through an Emax function of the PMB
concentration (Eq 5), and it raises the rate at which minocycline-induced
adaptive resistance develops through a power function of the PMB concentration
(Eq 10). The reverse (minocycline affecting PMB) was not supported.

Two clinical isolates were studied, and the paper is contributed to
nlmixr2lib as **two model files**, one per isolate:

```{r model-list}
olsson_models <- c(
  "Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU705",
  "Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU613"
)
strain_label <- c(
  Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU705 = "ARU705 (KPC-3)",
  Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU613 = "ARU613 (OXA-48)"
)
uis <- lapply(olsson_models, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
names(uis) <- olsson_models
lapply(uis, function(u) u$description)
```

ARU705 (KPC-3-producing; PMB MIC 0.5 mg/L, MIN MIC 1 mg/L) was the more
susceptible strain. Olsson 2024 generated strain-specific drug-effect
parameters for ARU705 from fresh static time-kill experiments, expressing them
as **scaling factors** on the ARU613 estimates (Table 3 footnote b: "the
estimated Slope1 for ARU705 for MIN single drug is 0.339 x 1.55 = 0.525"). The
ARU705 model file carries those scaling factors explicitly and multiplies them
by the ARU613 values; parameters not re-estimated for ARU705 (the Hill-type
exponents, the adaptive-resistance slopes, and the interaction `Slope4`,
`gamma4` and `Emax`) keep their ARU613 values.

ARU613 (OXA-48-producing) was non-susceptible to both drugs (PMB MIC 8 mg/L,
MIN MIC 8 mg/L) and carries the original Zhao 2020 model parameters.

# Population (biological context)

```{r population}
pop705 <- uis[["Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU705"]]$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Species", "Organism", "Model system", "Dose range"),
  Value = c(pop705$species, pop705$organism, pop705$model_system, pop705$dose_range)
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Both strains were resistant to meropenem and produced carbapenemases (ARU705
carried *bla*KPC-3, ARU613 carried *bla*OXA-48). The drug-effect parameters
derive from static time-kill experiments at a 6 log10 CFU/mL inoculum; Olsson
2024 then used the model to predict 72 h dynamic time-kill experiments in a
100 mL in vitro PK/PD apparatus mimicking free plasma concentrations in
critically ill patients.

# Source trace

Every parameter in both files is traced in an in-file comment to Table 3 of
Olsson 2024 (which, for ARU613, reproduces the Zhao 2020 static-model
estimates). The model structure is supplementary Table S1.

| Element | Source location |
|---|---|
| ODE structure (S, R, adaptive resistance) | Table S1, Eqs 1-3, 7-8 |
| Power-function kill rates (Eq 4), PMB-on-MIN Emax (Eq 5) | Table S1 |
| Adaptive-resistance inhibition, beta = +1 PMB / -1 MIN (Eq 6) | Table S1 |
| Adaptive-resistance on-rates (Eq 9), PMB-on-MIN power term (Eq 10) | Table S1 |
| `kgrowth`, `kdeath`, `Bmax`, `Tlag` | Table 3, "Bacteria-related" block |
| `Slope1`/`Slope2`/`gamma1`/`Slope3` per drug | Table 3, "Single drug-specific" block |
| `Emax`/`EC50`/`Slope4`/`gamma4` interaction | Table 3, "Combination-specific interaction" block |
| ARU705 scaling factors on Slope1/Slope2/EC50 | Table 3, ARU705 columns + footnote b |
| Inoculum 6 log10 CFU/mL | Methods, "PD predictions" |

```{r source-trace-readback}
# Read the transcribed constants back out of the built ARU613 model and confirm
# the key Table 3 values are present exactly as published.
ini613 <- uis[["Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU613"]]$iniDf
val <- function(nm) ini613$est[ini613$name == nm]
stopifnot(
  val("kgrowth") == 1.37,
  val("kdeath") == 0.179,
  val("log10bmax") == 9.53,
  val("tlag") == 0.304,
  val("slope1_pmb") == 0.0690,
  val("gamma1_pmb") == 1.20,
  val("slope1_mino") == 0.339,
  val("gamma1_mino") == 0.546,
  val("emax_int") == 2.45,
  val("ec50_int") == 0.285
)

# ARU705: Slope1 scaling reproduces the footnote-b worked example (0.339 x 1.55).
ini705 <- uis[["Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU705"]]$iniDf
v705 <- function(nm) ini705$est[ini705$name == nm]
stopifnot(
  # Footnote b rounds 0.339 x 1.55 to 0.525; the product is 0.52545.
  abs(v705("slope1_mino") * v705("fslope1_mino") - 0.525) < 1e-3,
  v705("fslope1_pmb") == 57.1,
  v705("fslope2_pmb") == 50.4,
  v705("fec50_int") == 0.553
)
```

# Helper: static time-kill simulation

A static time-kill experiment holds each drug at a constant bath concentration.
In these models the concentration lives in a state (`cpmb`, `cmino`) whose
derivative is zero, so a single dose event at time 0 fixes it for the run.

```{r static-helper}
simulate_static <- function(ui, pmb, mino, times = c(0, 2, 4, 8, 24)) {
  obs <- data.frame(time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "bact_susceptible")
  dose <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = 0, amt = pmb, evid = 1, cmt = "cpmb"),
    data.frame(time = 0, amt = mino, evid = 1, cmt = "cmino")
  )
  ev <- dplyr::arrange(dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs), time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  # rxSolve() returns one row per observation record and carries no `evid`
  # column, so select the output columns directly rather than filtering on evid.
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  out[, c("time", "log_cfu")]
}
```

# Static time-kill behaviour (replicates Figure 1 for ARU705)

Figure 1 of Olsson 2024 shows the static time-kill VPC for ARU705. The model
is deterministic here (typical values only), so we reproduce the structural
trends: a susceptible strain cleared by low PMB, concentration-dependent
regrowth at the higher single-drug PMB levels as adaptive resistance develops,
minocycline holding the count down but not clearing it, and the combination
driving the fastest and deepest kill.

```{r static-aru705}
ui705 <- uis[["Olsson_2024_polymyxinB_minocycline_ARU705"]]
scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,                 ~pmb, ~mino,
  "GC",                      0,     0,
  "PMB 0.5",                0.5,    0,
  "PMB 2",                   2,     0,
  "MIN 8",                   0,     8,
  "MIN 64",                  0,    64,
  "PMB 0.5 + MIN 1",        0.5,    1,
  "PMB 0.5 + MIN 4",        0.5,    4
)
static705 <- scenarios |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(label = label, simulate_static(ui705, pmb, mino))

ggplot(static705, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = expression(log[10] ~ "CFU/mL"),
    colour = NULL,
    title = "ARU705 static time-kill (typical-value predictions; cf. Figure 1)"
  )
```

```{r static-aru705-gates}
# Structural gates on the ARU705 static predictions (Figure 1 panels):
# the growth control saturates near Bmax, low PMB alone clears to the LOD,
# and the combination is the most bactericidal at 24 h.
gc24 <- static705$log_cfu[static705$label == "GC" & static705$time == 24]
pmb05_8 <- static705$log_cfu[static705$label == "PMB 0.5" & static705$time == 8]
comb24 <- static705$log_cfu[static705$label == "PMB 0.5 + MIN 4" & static705$time == 24]
min64_24 <- static705$log_cfu[static705$label == "MIN 64" & static705$time == 24]
stopifnot(
  gc24 > 9,                 # growth control reaches carrying capacity
  pmb05_8 < 7,              # 0.5 mg/L PMB (= MIC) kills early
  comb24 < min64_24,        # combination beats minocycline monotherapy
  comb24 < 2                # combination essentially clears the susceptible pool
)
```

# Dynamic time-kill predictions (replicates Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the model's in silico predictions for the 72 h dynamic
experiments that mimic patient plasma PK. We reconstruct the concentration
drivers from the paper's design (Methods, "Design of PK profiles"): targeted
peaks of 5.0 mg/L (loading) and 4.5 mg/L (maintenance) for PMB and 3.8 / 4.1
mg/L for minocycline, q12h dosing, with a biphasic elimination whose
half-lives are ~2 h for the first 3 h (first dose) / 2 h (subsequent doses) and
~10 h thereafter, and a constant 1.2 mg/L minocycline floor in the diluent.

```{r dynamic-driver}
# Per-cycle flow rate: fast phase (t<2 h into the cycle, 3 h for the first dose)
# then slow phase, as elimination half-lives of 2 and 10 h.
k_fast <- log(2) / 2
k_slow <- log(2) / 10

# Dose increments to hit the targeted peaks given the trough each cycle reaches.
pk_amts <- function(cmax_ld, cmax_md, floor) {
  tr_ld <- floor + (cmax_ld - floor) * exp(-3 * k_fast - 9 * k_slow)
  tr_md <- floor + (cmax_md - floor) * exp(-2 * k_fast - 10 * k_slow)
  c(cmax_ld, cmax_md - tr_ld, rep(cmax_md - tr_md, 4))
}
amt_pmb <- pk_amts(5.0, 4.5, 0)
amt_min <- pk_amts(3.8, 4.1, 1.2)

# Replace the zero `cpmb` / `cmino` derivatives with the biphasic washout. The
# numeric constants are inlined with sprintf so they do not become model
# parameters (rxode2::model() would otherwise treat k_slow etc. as thetas).
add_dynamic_pk <- function(ui, cmino_floor) {
  kflow <- sprintf(
    "(%.7f + %.7f * ((t < 3) + (t >= 12) * ((t - 12 * floor(t / 12)) < 2)))",
    k_slow, k_fast - k_slow
  )
  # Assign the parsed expressions to variables: rxode2::model() captures its
  # `...` by non-standard evaluation, so an inline str2lang(...) call would be
  # taken literally; a variable holding a language object is evaluated.
  pmb_ode <- str2lang(sprintf("d/dt(cpmb) <- -%s * cpmb", kflow))
  mino_ode <- str2lang(sprintf("d/dt(cmino) <- -%s * (cmino - %.4f)", kflow, cmino_floor))
  ui <- rxode2::model(ui, pmb_ode)
  rxode2::model(ui, mino_ode)
}

simulate_dynamic <- function(ui, pmb_on, min_on) {
  floor <- if (min_on) 1.2 else 0
  m <- add_dynamic_pk(ui, floor)
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.25), amt = 0, evid = 0,
                   cmt = "bact_susceptible")
  if (pmb_on) {
    ev <- rbind(ev, data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 60, 12), amt = amt_pmb,
                               evid = 1, cmt = "cpmb"))
  }
  if (min_on) {
    ev <- rbind(ev, data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 60, 12), amt = amt_min,
                               evid = 1, cmt = "cmino"))
  }
  ev <- ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev, returnType = "data.frame",
                                       maxsteps = 1e6))
  out[, c("time", "log_cfu")]
}
```

```{r dynamic-sim}
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,         ~pmb_on, ~min_on,
  "GC",           FALSE,   FALSE,
  "MIN",          FALSE,    TRUE,
  "PMB",           TRUE,   FALSE,
  "PMB + MIN",     TRUE,    TRUE
)

dynamic_all <- lapply(names(uis), function(nm) {
  ui <- uis[[nm]]
  res <- arms |>
    dplyr::rowwise() |>
    dplyr::reframe(arm = arm, simulate_dynamic(ui, pmb_on, min_on))
  res$strain <- strain_label[[nm]]
  res
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

ggplot(dynamic_all, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~strain) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, 8), linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 10)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = expression(log[10] ~ "CFU/mL"), colour = NULL,
    title = "Dynamic time-kill in silico predictions (cf. Figure 2)"
  )
```

The predicted curves reproduce the paper's headline findings. Read off Figure
2, the in silico lines pass through (log10 CFU/mL, +/- the line width):

* ARU705 (Figure 2a): minocycline ~8.3 at 12 h and ~9.3 at 24 h; polymyxin B
  ~1.0 to 12 h then regrowth to ~9.6 by ~30 h; the combination held at the LOD
  throughout.
* ARU613 (Figure 2b): the combination dips to ~5 at 8-12 h, then regrows,
  crossing ~8 at ~36 h and reaching ~9.3 by 48 h; single drugs track the
  growth control.

```{r dynamic-gates}
pick <- function(strain, arm, t) {
  d <- dynamic_all[dynamic_all$strain == strain & dynamic_all$arm == arm, ]
  d$log_cfu[which.min(abs(d$time - t))]
}

# ARU705: combination suppresses to the LOD and stays there; PMB alone regrows.
stopifnot(
  pick("ARU705 (KPC-3)", "PMB + MIN", 24) < 1,
  pick("ARU705 (KPC-3)", "PMB + MIN", 72) < 1,
  pick("ARU705 (KPC-3)", "PMB", 12) < 2,        # PMB nadir before regrowth
  pick("ARU705 (KPC-3)", "PMB", 48) > 8,        # PMB regrowth
  pick("ARU705 (KPC-3)", "MIN", 24) > 8         # minocycline does not clear
)

# ARU613: combination dips then regrows (synergy only transient); the 12 h and
# 48 h values bracket the Figure 2b trajectory.
comb613_12 <- pick("ARU613 (OXA-48)", "PMB + MIN", 12)
comb613_48 <- pick("ARU613 (OXA-48)", "PMB + MIN", 48)
stopifnot(
  comb613_12 > 4, comb613_12 < 7,               # transient suppression ~5-6.5
  comb613_48 > 8,                               # full regrowth by 48 h
  comb613_48 > comb613_12                        # regrowth, not sustained kill
)
```

# Adaptive resistance drives the ARU705 polymyxin B regrowth

The sharp PMB-alone regrowth against ARU705 is the model's irreversible
adaptive resistance: `aron_pmb` climbs toward 1 under PMB exposure, and the
inhibition factor `1 - Slope3 * aron_pmb` (Slope3 = 1 for PMB) drives the PMB
kill rate toward zero. We confirm the mechanism by reading the state back.

```{r ar-mechanism}
m705 <- add_dynamic_pk(ui705, 0)
ev <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.5), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "bact_susceptible"),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 60, 12), amt = amt_pmb, evid = 1, cmt = "cpmb")
)
ev <- ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
ar <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m705, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
ar_on_24 <- ar$aron_pmb[which.min(abs(ar$time - 24))]
# By 24 h adaptive resistance has developed substantially, abolishing PMB kill.
stopifnot(ar_on_24 > 0.9, all(ar$aron_pmb >= -1e-9), all(ar$aron_pmb <= 1 + 1e-9))
ar_on_24
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No residual error or between-experiment variability.** Olsson 2024 reports
  typical-value parameters only (Table 3); the original Zhao 2020 fit, which
  would carry the residual model and any between-experiment variability, is not
  open access and has been queued for future acquisition. `addSd` is therefore
  `fixed(0)` and the models are deterministic. The static VPC of Figure 1
  (grey shaded 95% interval) cannot be reproduced without that variance model;
  this vignette compares against the Figure 1 **medians** and the Figure 2
  prediction lines.
* **ARU705 static predictions are more bactericidal than the Figure 1 VPC at
  low drug concentrations.** The typical-value model clears 0.5-2 mg/L PMB to
  well below the LOD within hours, whereas the Figure 1 VPC medians regrow at
  those levels. This reflects a known limitation the authors discuss (static
  24 h data under-predict the late regrowth and resistance seen over longer
  experiments). The structural gates above are written on the robust features
  (growth-control saturation, combination being the most bactericidal), not on
  the extreme low-concentration kill depth.
* **Dynamic concentration drivers are reconstructed, not transcribed.** The
  paper gives targeted peaks/troughs, phase half-lives, the phase-switch times,
  and the minocycline diluent floor (Methods, "Design of PK profiles"; Figure
  S2), but not a closed-form concentration equation. The biphasic
  exponential-washout driver here reproduces the targeted Figure S2 profiles
  (PMB peaks ~4.5-5, troughs ~1.1; minocycline peaks ~3.8-4.1, troughs ~1.8
  with a 1.2 mg/L floor). Simulations that need the exact measured
  concentrations should supply them as a time-course into `cpmb` / `cmino`.
* **Irreversible adaptive resistance.** Table S1 gives no return (`koff`) term
  for either `aron` state, so `aroff -> aron` is one-way; the `aron` states
  therefore accumulate monotonically toward 1 over an experiment.
* **S -> R transfer switches on at `Tlag`.** Eq 3 sets the transfer rate to 0
  for `Time < Tlag`; here `Tlag` = 0.304 h is small, so the switch is near the
  start of the run.
```
